chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Some people praised him to his face,
then he said: O My God! You know me better than myself, and I know myself better than they do. O My God! Make us better than what they think and forgive us what they do not know.

key_terms.فِى وَجْهِهِ: to his face / in his presence

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali respond to being praised to his face?
ai.summary: This saying highlights the Shia concept of *al-‘Ilm al-Ilahi* (Divine Knowledge) versus human conjecture, where the Imam acknowledges that while he knows his own inner state, only God knows the unseen realities of his heart. It serves as a model for spiritual humility, distinguishing between the praise of the masses (*al-nas*) and the judgment of the All-Knowing (*Allah*), reinforcing the idea that true worth is determined by divine assessment rather than public opinion. This supplication also reflects the Imam's awareness of potential hidden flaws (*khawa’if*) that even he might not fully perceive, seeking forgiveness for what is unknown to both him and the people.
